text:
ada: Heads-up — saw a short spike of apiserver 5xxs in eu-west1 around 08:12 UTC while the GPU provisioner was onboarding a new pool. Controller-manager restarted twice and leader flipped.

miguel: on it, can you paste the apiserver logs or the tail of the kube-apiserver pod? suspecting conn spikes + watch fanout.

ada: pasted logs below. noticed lots of `watch` reconnects + `io timeout` from proxy. only during the onboarding wave.
```
E0812 08:12:21.123456 1 handler.go:200] apiserver request error: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
E0812 08:12:21.123789 1 logs.go:98] watch-stream: client x.x.x.x disconnected: net/http: timeout awaiting response headers
```

leah: graphs show apiserver lat p95 jump to ~1.8s for ~2m and controller-manager queue depth spiked. provisioner attach latency also increased.

sam: is this tied to NAT / SNAT exhaustion again? onboarding + k8s watch fanning = conn churn. eu-west had a brief NAT port pool pressure at 08:10.

miguel: good point. can we confirm conntrack / SNAT metrics on the nat-gateway for that window? also check controller-manager leader election logs for lease timeouts.

ada: controller-manager logs show renew failures: `failed to update lease: net/http: request canceled` a few times before restart.

leah: mitigation plan: 1) throttle provisioner concurrency to 5 for the in-flight pool, 2) enable ephemeral fallback to reserve partial GPU capacity, 3) bump controller-manager lease duration temporarily to 45s. thoughts?

sam: thumbs up for throttling. I'll open a short-lived cloud NAT scale (add extra ports) and lower provisioner concurrency; that should stop new watch spikes.

miguel: runbook ops — to throttle provisioner:
```
kubectl -n infra patch deploy/gpu-provisioner -p '{"spec":{"replicas":1}}'
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/gpu-provisioner PROV_CONCURRENCY=5
```

leah: I'm patching controller-manager lease values now (canary):
```
kubectl -n kube-system edit deployment controller-manager
# set --leader-elect-lease-duration=45s --leader-elect-renew-deadline=30s
```

sre-bot: Alert suppressed for eu-west1 apiserver 5xx spike (window=10m) — suppression set by @sam while mitigation ongoing. :white_check_mark:

ada: after throttling + short NAT scale we saw error rate drop within 90s and controller-manager stabilized. still want a follow-up: runbook + long-term fix (prefix NAT, reduce watch fanout, use informer caches, or apply gateway autoscaling).

miguel: agree. I'll capture the graphs and open an RFC for: better provisioner backoff, circuit-breaker on watch storms, and NAT capacity autoscale. tagging @platform and @networking for cost/infra tradeoffs.

leah: filing an incident note and a short postmortem ticket. assigning remediation: limit simultaneous GPU attach ops per region, add early KV cache priming for controllers, and investigate multi-NAT redundancy.

sam: cost note — temporary NAT port increases are cheap compared to repeated controlplane restarts. we should quantify for proposal.

ada: thanks everyone — system is stable now. leaving this thread open for the next 24h for any regressions.
